data.title: Calif. Gov. Newsom issues executive order to develop AI kill switch
data.description:
Calif. Gov. Gavin Newsom issued an executive order on Friday to establish an independent oversight of AI companies and to develop an artificial intelligence kill switch.

The order calls for the creation of a panel of experts within the next two months to help the state reinforce and strengthen its AI regulations. It also requires AI companies to create a "kill switch for frontier models, with the efficacy of the switch verified on an ongoing basis by an independent verification organization."

The order comes out after a raucous week of national debate on the potential dangers of ever-improving AI models. Last week, Anthropic (ANTHRO) CEO Dario Amodei said that the progress of improving AI model capabilities should be slowed down. What's more, a former researcher at OpenAI (OPENAI) and Anthropic took to social media and news outlets to warn civilization of the possible impending doom related to frontier AI model development. The post prompted Evan Hubinger, Alignment Science Lead at Anthropic, to respond.

"Jacob is correct here—we really do earnestly believe AI could kill all humans," he said. "I, personally, think it is >10% within the next decade."

U.S. President Donald Trump entered the fray, encouraging AI firms to proceed full steam ahead. 

"There is a SICK conspiracy going on against AI and data centers, and the only one that is happy about it is China," he posted on Truth Social. "WHOEVER WINS AI, WINS! We are leading China, and all others, and will continue to do so."

The executive order also follows the infamous Hugging Face attack that was carried out by an army of AI agents running on OpenAI's models.

"The federal government's abject failure to create any form of meaningful AI oversight or accountability should alarm every American, especially when AI CEOs themselves are begging for regulation," Newsom said. "We're not waiting to act—we're going to speed up our work on substantial and responsible AI oversight before it's too late. We're going to do this thoughtfully but with urgent velocity; the stakes are too high to wait or delay action." 

"While Washington abdicates its responsibility to protect Americans, California is building on the strongest AI regulatory framework in the nation," he added. "California has already built a national model, and our policy should be the national baseline."

data.title: Midday Need to Know: Buffett exits Berkshire chair role, crypto stocks rise & more
data.description:
The stock market slipped Friday as Treasury yields reversed Thursday's retreat, with the 10-year note climbing back to the key 5.0% mark.

The S&P 500 (SP500) -0.2%, the Dow (DJI) -0.4%, and the Nasdaq Composite (COMP:IND) was virtually flat.

Now, here are 4 news stories that broke in the morning to watch out for:

Warren Buffett steps down as Berkshire Hathaway chairman: The 96-year-old billionaire is  relinquishing the chairman role after 61 years, becoming chairman emeritus while remaining on the board. His son Howard G. Buffett, a 33-year board veteran, has been named chairman, while Greg Abel continues as CEO after succeeding Warren Buffett in that role less than a year ago. "Father Time always wins," Buffett wrote in a letter to shareholders, adding that he is "more confident than ever about what lies ahead" for the conglomerate he transformed from a failing textiles business into an insurance powerhouse with a nearly $300B equities portfolio. 

SEC approves temporary exemption for tokenized stock trading: U.S. crypto-related stocks  extended gains after the Securities and Exchange Commission approved a five-year "Innovation Exemption" allowing certain platforms to facilitate trading of tokenized versions of U.S.-listed securities. Strategy rose 7%, MARA Holdings gained 6%, and Coinbase Global, Galaxy Digital, and Circle Internet Group each climbed roughly 6%. The exemption permits tokenized securities venues to trade National Market System stocks through permissioned automated market makers and liquidity pools, subject to volume and symbol limits. 

Fed to finalize bank stress test and capital reforms: Federal Reserve Vice Chair for Supervision Michelle Bowman  announced the Fed board will consider final revisions to its stress testing framework in coming weeks. The changes aim to improve transparency, strengthen model reliability, and reduce volatility in capital requirements. One final rule would require publishing detailed stress test model information, while another would average a bank's two most recent annual stress test results to smooth the stress capital buffer requirement. The effective date for new requirements would shift to January 1 from October 1.

Treasury weighs allowing most China biopharma licensing deals: The U.S. Treasury Department is  formulating rules expected to permit American drugmakers to continue investing in cutting-edge Chinese-developed medicines, excluding biotechnology that could be weaponized, Reuters reported. The rules have not been finalized and may be amended, particularly if President Donald Trump intervenes ahead of next week's meeting between Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping. Major drugmakers including Pfizer have lobbied against broad restrictions, with CEO Albert Bourla arguing that blocking access to Chinese innovations is not the way to compete.

data.title: Boeing selloff on CEO comments an 'overreaction,' BofA says
data.description:
Boeing's (BA) recent two-day slide following remarks from CEO Kelly Ortberg at a Morgan Stanley conference is an "overreaction to predictable headwinds," Bank of America said in a note Friday, reiterating its Buy rating and $270 price target.

Boeing (BA) "operates in a complex, highly regulated industry, and its execution was seriously compromised so it will naturally take time, but the turnaround is broadly progressing in the right direction," BofA analyst Ronald Epstein wrote, adding that the company's improvements compared to a year ago are "noticeable."

The company is taking longer than expected to stabilize production of the 737 MAX at 47 aircraft per month, Ortberg said, but the analyst responded that "this isn't surprising, as accelerating production of anything has growing pains, but for somethting as large and complex as an airplane, it is a little harder," and Boeing's (BA) broader supply chain remains "solid."

Separately, the Federal Aviation Administration proposed a new airworthiness directive Friday for certain Boeing (BA) 737-8, 737-9, and 737-8200 jets, prompted by reports indicating cracks in the bear strap and stub frame at the forward galley door cutout.

The directive requires "detailed inspections of the elevator buss assembly bearings and bearing housings for any crack and indication of sealant application, and applicable on-condition actions," according to a notice posted in the Federal Register.

data.title: Inflation should be the main focus of monetary policy, Kansas City Fed's Schmid says
data.description:
Kansas City Fed President Jeffrey Schmid supported the Federal Open Market Committee's decision to raise the federal funds rate target range by 25 basis points to 3.75%-4.00% on Wednesday, he said on Friday. The move was the first hike in more than three years, as inflation has outpaced the Fed's 2% goal for more than five years.

"In tightening policy, the FOMC was responding to inflation that has remained too high for too long," he said in a speech at the Independent Community Bankers of Colorado annual convention in Vail, Colorado.

Oil prices have been a key driver of the higher inflation, he said, but it's not the only driver. "Inflation excluding energy has also been running hot, and a broad range of goods and services are showing price growth inconsistent with our price stability target," he said in the text he prepared for the event.

"High inflation is a signal that the economy is out of balance, and the Fed, through its influence on demand, always has a role to play when it comes to keeping inflation in check," Schmid noted.

The U.S. economy's strength has given the Fed room to raise interest rates without damaging the labor market.

"Overall economic growth is solid, supported by continued consumer spending and strong business investment," said Schmid, who is not a voting member of the FOMC this year. "With the labor market in balance and growth resilient, inflation is my primary concern as I think about the correct course for monetary policy."

data.title: Treasury yields rebound as markets weigh further Fed hikes
data.description:
U.S. Treasury yields rebounded Friday after pulling back in the previous session, as markets continued to assess the prospect of further Federal Reserve rate increases following this week's hike.

The 2-year Treasury yield (US2Y) rose 6.5 basis points to 4.75%, while the 5-year yield (US5Y) gained 6.9 basis points to 4.86%. The 10-year yield (US10Y) climbed 6.8 basis points to 5.01%, and the 30-year yield (US30Y) advanced 4.7 basis points to 5.34%.

The move came after yields fell Thursday. The 2-year yield declined 6 basis points to 4.67%, while the 10-year yield slipped 9 basis points to 4.93%, and the 30-year yield fell 8 basis points to 5.28%.

The Federal Open Market Committee increased its benchmark interest rate by 25 basis points on Wednesday, as widely expected, marking the first rate hike in more than three years.

Treasuries came under renewed pressure as investors weighed the prospect of additional Federal Reserve rate increases. The move was more pronounced in shorter-maturity debt, with the 2-year yield reaching 4.75%.

Investors also increased wagers on higher yields for short-maturity debt, while comments from Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh were interpreted as suggesting that at least one additional rate increase could come this year, according to Bloomberg.

Kalshi contracts showed a 73% chance of the 10-year Treasury yield being at or above 4.75% at year-end, up 13 percentage points. The market showed a 58% chance of the yield reaching at least 5%, up 10 percentage points, while the odds of at least 5.1% stood at 32% and at least 5.15% at 29%.

Cue Biopharma is a new Buy at B. Riley on valuation
data.description:
Cue Biopharma (CUE) traded higher as the markets opened on Friday after B. Riley Securities launched its coverage with a Buy recommendation, noting that the company’s valuation doesn’t reflect its experimental drugs, CUE-221 and CUE-401.

With the stock implying approximately $234M in enterprise value, “we believe the shares reflect neither,” analyst Mayank Mamtani argued, issuing a 12-month price target of $83 on CUE.

Mamtani noted that Cue’s (CUE) near-term opportunity lies in allergy, for which its lead asset, CUE-221, is currently in Phase 2 development. The anti-IgE antibody is undergoing a Phase 2 clinical trial in China sponsored by its licensor, Ascendent Health, for a skin condition called "chronic spontaneous urticaria," with results expected by the end of Q3 2026.

“We view it as a dose selection and mechanism test, not a superiority trial, and a supportive result opens a global Ph2b in food allergy, where 33M Americans have one approved drug and where the two prior commercial attempts, Aimmune's Palforzia and DBV's patch, failed or stalled on delivery burden, not efficacy,” Mamtani wrote.

Cue’s (CUE) lead autoimmune candidate CUE-401, which is set to enter Phase 1 development following an investigational new drug application (IND) expected by the end of this year, represents the company’s “long-term upside," the analyst added.
